transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-02-16 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Markus Vogel (Lumina Head of Security), Aisha Rahman (Lumina CTO), Diego Marquez (Platform)

Summary:
Lumina is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted + private (VPC) deployments. Primary focus is security posture: SOC2/ISO certs, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logs, encryption (KMS/BYOK/HSM), and data retention/e-discovery. They are leaning towards Dedicated for latency-sensitive pipelines but need onboarding plan and pen-test evidence for Private on-prem option.

Topics covered:
- SOC2 / ISO27001 certification and recent pen test
- SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning timeline and RBAC model
- Audit, event logs, SIEM integration (Splunk) and retention windows
- Encryption at rest: KMS, BYOK, HSM options and key rotation
- Data residency, egress controls and VPC peering / private deployments
- Dedicated capacity benchmarking and fallback strategies

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Jared Kim: Hey team, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side, I'm Jared, AE, and Priya is our SE who's going to go into the nitty gritty for security and deployment.
[00:00:12] Markus Vogel: Thanks Jared. Markus here. we're trying to map out the infosec roadmap for inference across our product lines. A lot of this will impact SRE and legal.
[00:00:20] Aisha Rahman: Hi all. yes, we want a clear path for SOC2 and to understand if Redwood Dedicated or Private fits best for our regulated datasets.
[00:00:00] Priya Shah: great, can I quickly confirm the scope? You said regulated customer data, are we talking PII and PCI-lite, or more healthcare PHI?
[00:00:38] Diego Marquez: Mainly PII and some PHI in a subset of pipelines. we want encryption, auditability, and strict retention windows — 7 years for some records, 1 year for others.
[00:00:47] Priya Shah: understood. on the SOC2 piece, we are SOC2 Type II compliant — we can share the report. we also have an ISO27001 certificate. i can send the certs and our most recent pen test summary after the call.
[00:01:05] Markus Vogel: that would be great. the pen test you'll send, does it include red team exercises and 3rd party assessor?
[00:01:12] Jared Kim: yes, our pen test is by a third party assessor. i'll include the scope doc so you can see what was in- and out-of-scope.
[00:01:20] Aisha Rahman: For SSO, we currently use Okta, and we need SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning. we also want role-sync for groups from Okta to map to product RBAC.
[00:01:30] Priya Shah: Redwood supports SAML and SCIM. our RBAC model is flexible — you can map groups to roles, and we support token-level scopes. small caveat: if you go private with a customer-managed control plane there are a couple of extra steps for SCIM SC integration.
[00:01:45] Diego Marquez: can you detail the extra steps? we try to avoid manual sync.
[00:01:50] Priya Shah: sure, on private control plane there is an initial bootstrap where SCIM endpoints are configured in your IdP and we provide a service account for provisioning. after that it's automated. sometimes the attribute mapping needs a quick patch depending on how custom your Okta schema is.
[00:02:10] Markus Vogel: audit logs are critical. what's the max retention out of the box? and do you stream to Splunk or S3?
[00:02:18] Priya Shah: by default audit logs are retained 90 days in the console. we support forwarding logs to customer Splunk or to an S3 bucket (encrypted at rest). for longer retention you can configure log forwarding or provision a private deployment and manage retention on your side.
[00:02:37] Aisha Rahman: do logs include raw prompt/response payloads? we have concerns about PHI in prompts.
[00:02:45] Jared Kim: good question — by default we redact full request bodies from console-level audit trails. for customers who need full telemetry for debugging, we can enable verbose logs but we'd recommend routing those to a secured S3 with stricter access controls and shorter retention.
[00:03:05] Diego Marquez: ok that helps. what about encryption keys? we have a BYOK policy and need HSM-backed keys for production.
[00:03:12] Priya Shah: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via major cloud KMS providers. for Dedicated and Private on cloud regions we can integrate with your KMS; for a full on-prem air-gapped deployment we support HSMs via a supported connector. key rotation can be scheduled and we provide rotation logs.
[00:03:33] Markus Vogel: is there any shared-key material on Redwood side for session caching or KV cache? we need to ensure our keys never leave our KMS.
[00:03:41] Priya Shah: good note — Redis/KV cache used for inference cacheable prefixes is encrypted at rest; for Private deployments the caching layer can be inside your VPC and uses your KMS for disk encryption. small transcription aside: sometimes docs show KV as 'K V cache' in auto-captioning.
[00:03:57] Aisha Rahman: network egress is also a blocker. our data classification says no egress to public internet for certain buckets. can Redwood live in our VPC and never talk publicly?
[00:04:07] Priya Shah: yes. Private deployment supports VPC peering and egress controls. we can do private endpoints only; there are options for NAT-less setups but that increases operational complexity.
[00:04:20] Diego Marquez: timeline wise, how long to stand up a VPC private control plane?
[00:04:26] Jared Kim: typically 4–6 weeks for the control plane and endpoints, assuming access and network approvals. Dedicated pools are much faster — you can be up in 1–2 weeks.
[00:04:35] Markus Vogel: and compliance evidence — can we get continuous compliance logs and a SOC2 / ISO artifact repository?
[00:04:42] Priya Shah: yes we have an artifacts package for enterprise customers — SOC2 report, ISO certificate, architecture diagrams, encryption key handling docs, and pen test summary. we also provide an audit log export and a compliance runbook for security teams.
[00:04:56] Aisha Rahman: we need RBAC to integrate with our internal approval gating. do you have fine-grained roles and separation of duties?
[00:05:04] Priya Shah: we do. there's admin, billing, deployer, auditor roles and you can create custom roles. actions are mapped to permissions so you can enforce separation of duties.
[00:05:15] Markus Vogel: do you support per-team model pinning and per-token cost tagging for audit?
[00:05:22] Priya Shah: yes — cost/latency tagging is available, and model pinning can be set per-org or per-team. logs carry token-level metadata for billing and auditing.
[00:05:35] Diego Marquez: one question about backups and deletion: if we delete a dataset, is there a safe-delete or hard-delete? we have legal holds sometimes.
[00:05:42] Priya Shah: we offer configurable retention and deletion policies. there's soft-delete (recoverable for X days) and hard-delete. for legal hold scenarios we can integrate with your e-discovery workflow, and we keep immutable logs indicating deletion requests.
[00:06:00] Aisha Rahman: could you walk through a hypothetical flow: customer uploads training prompts to a private dedicated pool, inference runs, logs go to Splunk, keys in our KMS — how are tokens and responses handled?
[00:06:12] Priya Shah: high level — data stays inside your VPC if Private: requests ingress through private endpoints, inference executes on your dedicated GPUs, KV cache and model sharding happen inside private subnets, logs are forwarded to your Splunk via a secure connector, and encryption keys never leave your KMS. we do ephemeral caches and support TTLs so sensitive prompts do not persist longer than necessary.
[00:06:35] Markus Vogel: any export of model artifacts? we do not want any model snapshots leaving our environment.
[00:06:40] Priya Shah: for Private it's entirely customer-controlled — we don't snapshot or export model weights from your environment. for hosted variants we use model variants but customer data is not included in our model training.
[00:06:55] Diego Marquez: what about regulatory audits — can Redwood team support an on-site audit or remote evidence collection?
[00:07:02] Jared Kim: we can provide remote evidence and dedicated audit packs. on-site audits are possible for Private deployments under an enterprise agreement with an NDA and scoping.
[00:07:15] Aisha Rahman: regarding SLA, do you have latency and availability numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:07:22] Priya Shah: Dedicated has SLA-backed throughput and P99 latency targets depending on the instance class; hosted is best-effort with published latency profiles. we'll share the SLA doc in follow up.
[00:07:34] Markus Vogel: penetration testing cadence — how often is that done? and do you have public CVE response processes?
[00:07:41] Priya Shah: annual pen tests and quarterly vuln scans, plus a standard incident response process. we publish CVE timelines to customers when relevant.
[00:07:52] Diego Marquez: integration with our SIEM (Splunk) — is it push or pull? do you provide a webhook or a forwarder?
[00:07:58] Priya Shah: we support both push forwarders to Splunk (using secure tokens) and S3 export that your Splunk can ingest. webhooks are available for event notifications.
[00:08:10] Markus Vogel: any particular gotchas for hybrid deployments where some teams are on Hosted and others on Private?
[00:08:16] Priya Shah: the main challenge is consistent RBAC and key management — we recommend centralizing key rotation in your KMS and centralizing identity (Okta) so SAML/SCIM maps cleanly across environments. also model parity; make sure you're pinning model versions across hosts to avoid drift.
[00:08:33] Aisha Rahman: cost controls — can we set max spend per team or per route?
[00:08:38] Priya Shah: yes, rate limits, quotas, and token-level budget alerts can be configured per-team. Dedicated usage is billed separately under reserved capacity.
[00:08:49] Diego Marquez: for the benchmark, what's the best test to emulate our workloads? we do short-chat and long-document summarization.
[00:08:56] Priya Shah: we'll run a mixed workload: 60% short chat (<=128 tokens), 40% long docs (~2k tokens) with KV cache warm-up scenarios. we'll also test prefix-caching and continuous batching to mirror production.
[00:09:12] Markus Vogel: any differences in how you handle telemetry for long doc workloads?
[00:09:16] Priya Shah: we capture token-level latency and KV hit rates. for long docs we recommend tuned kernels and quantization profiles; we'll include performance suggestions in the benchmark report.
[00:09:30] Aisha Rahman: one last thing — data residency. We have EU customers only. can you guarantee EU region-only hosting and restricted egress?
[00:09:38] Priya Shah: yes we can pin deployments to EU regions and apply routing policies to avoid cross-region egress. for strict residency with Private on-prem you control the physical location entirely.
[00:09:50] Markus Vogel: perfect. so next steps: share SOC docs, architecture, set up benchmark.
[00:09:56] Jared Kim: yep — i'll follow up with docs and calendar invites for the benchmark. thanks for the time.
[00:10:02] Aisha Rahman: thanks everyone, appreciated.
[00:42:00] <end of recording>

Notes on transcription artifacts: speaker labels occasionally default to "Speaker 1" in the raw file; some product names show as "Redwood Dedicate" or "K V cache" due to captioning errors. There was minor crosstalk at ~00:06:00 when Diego and Markus both interjected.
